These are executed in order.' — the constraint's order claim is doc-grounded, and 'per-operation results' is grounded via the api-reference (endpoint_registry doc_quote for points+batch: 'Operations are executed in order; returns 200 with per-operation results; 404 for a missing collection'); HOWEVER the doc says NOTHING about atomicity, rollback, or failure handling of a batch — the all-or-nothing premise the script's DEFECT requires is absent from this page (contrast: the aliases+update documentation explicitly promises 'alias operations are ATOMIC' — the docs differentiate the two faces). http_semantics.note: The poison op surfaced as request-level HTTP 400 with error body 'Wrong input: Vector dimension error: expected dim: 4, got 2' — but the 400 arrived AFTER the batch's prefix operations (602, 603) had already been submitted and applied (request used wait=true); for this endpoint a 4xx response therefore does not imply zero side effects. Inversion of the usual 2xx-masking pattern: correct error class, non-clean rejection.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: batch operations are applied sequentially in the order given; each operation reports its own result
contract_grounding.note: Recovered constraint_id (dispatch candidates.jsonl field was empty; named in script header line 6 and log DEFECT line 14) — found in structured_contract.json constraints.state_constraints. violates-declaration self-check: the observed phenomenon (rejected batch left its committed prefix) is OUTSIDE this assertion's constraint domain. The assertion promises (a) sequential in-order application — the observed behavior applies 602 then 603 then aborts at the poison, i.e. exactly in order; (b) per-op result reporting — a success-face promise (api-reference: 'returns 200 with per-operation results'), satisfied on the 200 CTL leg. The assertion nowhere promises all-or-nothing rollback, and no alternative constraint in the contract covers points+batch atomicity (checked all 28 state_constraints; the only explicit atomicity constraint, qdrant_state_aliases_update_001, is endpoint-specific to aliases+update). Wrong-constraint-cited branch of the self-check applies: either the citation must change to an atomicity constraint (none exists for this endpoint) or the behavior is compliant with the cited assertion — under the cited text it is compliant. The DEFECT verdict rests on an undocumented atomicity premise (reasonable transactional expectation, but not what this doc/constraint promises).

chain_trace.break_detail: The doc link does not carry the claim: the cited constraint is faithfully grounded in the doc ('executed in order'), but the doc prose contains no all-or-nothing/rollback promise for points+batch, so the claim's violated expectation (rejected batch => no state change) has no documentation anchor. The docs deliberately differentiate: aliases+update is documented ATOMIC; points+batch is documented only as ordered. Auditor should weigh: real, stable, source-confirmed non-atomic behavior, tested against a face whose documentation does not promise atomicity (compare sibling candidates anchored on qdrant_state_aliases_update_001, where the same behavior IS a documented-contract violation).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix route update_batch (src/actix/api/update_api.rs:327) -> do_batch_update_points (src/common/update.rs:752): (1) upfront loop checks ONLY strict-mode/quota for all ops (lines 762-770) — no upfront vector-dimension or cross-batch validation; (2) per-op for-loop (783-892) dispatches each UpdateOperation to do_upsert_points / do_update_vectors / etc., each ending with immediate '?' error propagation — first apply-time failure aborts the loop and returns Err for the whole request; (3) per-op do_* -> update() (src/common/update.rs:1201) -> toc.update submits to the shard update channel/WAL and, with wait=true, blocks until the operation is applied or fails; (4) the poison op's dimension check runs at apply time in the segment layer (lib/segment/src/common/mod.rs:188-219) raising OperationError::WrongVectorDimension (lib/segment/src/common/operation_error.rs:22-26), mapped to StorageError::BadInput 'Wrong input: ...' (lib/storage/src/content_manager/errors.rs:15-16) -> HTTP 400. NO rollback/compensation code exists anywhere in the batch path; already-applied prefix ops stay durable. Request-parse-time poisons (wrong op key) instead fail serde deserialization of the whole UpdateOperations body before any op runs — matching the sibling order_001 P3 observation (nothing applied). This structure implements 'executed in order' literally and contains no atomicity mechanism; no comment or docstring in the path declares non-atomicity intentional, so by_design_in_source is NOT available under the v3.4 tightening (bare structural behavior without explicit intent evidence).
